messages:
Kevin: Quick sync — we need final per-GPU `max_tokens_per_batch` and `max_batch_size` guidelines for continuous batching. Current defaults are blowing up on T4 in staging (OOMs). Anyone with the latest profiling numbers?

Ashwin: Posted a run from yesterday. High level first: different families behave very differently w.r.t KV cache and kernel selection. Raw recommended caps (baseline quantized models, 4-bit, typical chat traffic):
- A10: max_tokens_per_batch ~ 40_000, max_batch_size 64
- T4: max_tokens_per_batch ~ 12_000, max_batch_size 32
- L4: max_tokens_per_batch ~ 20_000, max_batch_size 48
- A100: max_tokens_per_batch ~ 80_000, max_batch_size 128
- H100: max_tokens_per_batch ~ 120_000, max_batch_size 192

These are *starting* points (memory headroom assumed ~10%). They are for steady-state throughput; tail-latency sensitive stacks should be lower.

Julia: Important caveat — when KV cache hit ratio drops (more new context per request) memory footprint increases ~20–30%. For chat-like long ctx, we should reduce tokens cap by ~20% compared to Ashwin's numbers. Example: T4 -> 10k tokens cap for chat.

Maria: FYI we hit a perf regression on H100 in the last rollout: p99 jumped 2x when token cap > 90k for the 70B family (KV pressure + kernel fallback). I reverted the config. @Ashwin can you attach the flamegraphs? :face_with_rolling_eyes:

Ashwin: Flamegraphs attached to the perf ticket (INF-421). TL;DR: kernel selector fell back to slower path when per-batch token budget caused sequence lengths to spike above 16k, which triggers a different attention kernel. Throughput/p99 numbers from the profiling run (single-GPU, mixed priority queue):
```
GPU   | tokens/sec | p99 latency (ms) | notes
A10   | 120k       | 95               | stable, mem headroom ~12%
T4    | 28k        | 140              | OOMs at >14k cap on 8GB unless batch_size limited
L4    | 60k        | 110              | sweet spot around 48 batch
A100  | 410k       | 60               | good for large batch tokens
H100  | 560k       | 75               | regressed when tok_cap > 90k (see INF-421)
```

Ashwin: Also tested dynamic kernel-selection impact: if average seq_len > 8k we often hit a fallback kernel that cuts throughput by ~30%. So the token cap has to be tuned with distribution, not just worst-case.

Samir: Suggestion for queue policy changes: prefer latency SLO -> when in high concurrency (>32 inflight batches) gate tokens-per-batch to 50% of configured cap, else allow full cap. Also add a soft token-bucket that drains on enqueue errors. Pseudoconfig: 
```
continuous_batching:
  per_gpu:
    T4: { max_batch_size: 32, max_tokens_per_batch: 12000 }
    A10: { max_batch_size: 64, max_tokens_per_batch: 40000 }
    L4: { max_batch_size: 48, max_tokens_per_batch: 20000 }
    A100: { max_batch_size: 128, max_tokens_per_batch: 80000 }
    H100: { max_batch_size: 192, max_tokens_per_batch: 90000 }
  queue_policy:
    concurrency_high_threshold: 32
    high_concurrency_token_factor: 0.5
    backpressure: token_bucket
```

Julia: +1 on the soft degradation. Also add an override per-model (especially for 70B family) to force kernel selection policy to use the high-memory-but-faster kernel when we have >16k seqs but only on A100/H100.

Maria: Action items: 1) Ashwin to open PR with per-GPU baseline config (use conservative H100 cap 90k). 2) Samir to prototype queue_policy token-bucket + concurrency gate. 3) Perf bot to run CI benchmarks against INF-421 workload. I can validate on staging after PR.

perf-bot: CI job continuous-batching-e2e/2026-03-16 completed: H100 scenario failed with tok_cap=120000 on main — see job logs (INF-421).

Kevin: Perfect — let's get the PRs and mark the rollout as canary only until we verify stable p99. Thanks everyone :rocket:
